title: Binomial Distribution of Successful Blocks
statement: Fix a natural number $q$ and a Boolean-valued test $B$ on Boolean lists. For natural numbers $K$ and $j$ with $j\le K$, divide a uniformly chosen Boolean string of length $Kq$ into $K$ consecutive blocks of length $q$, and count the blocks on which $B$ returns true. If $s$ is the fraction of length-$q$ Boolean strings on which $B$ returns true, then the probability that exactly $j$ blocks pass the test is $\binom Kj s^j(1-s)^{K-j}$.
hypotheses_covered: $B$ is a Boolean-valued test on Boolean lists
